title: Research 1/9: stare decisis mechanics - vertical vs horizontal precedent, mapped to agent role hierarchies
description: Research agenda item 1 of the roadmap brief (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:49). How do common-law systems determine which court's decisions bind which others - vertical precedent (appellate over lower) vs horizontal precedent (a court over its own future panels)? Cover at minimum: the hierarchy rule and its exceptions (per incuriam, conflicting prior authority, panel vs en banc), the binding/persuasive line for coordinate and foreign jurisdictions, and why the operative part binds while dicta do not. Then map it onto agent hierarchies: which agent-roles decisions bind which lineages. Output docs/precedent-research/01-stare-decisis-mechanics.md. Web research with named primary and secondary sources; every claim tagged ESTABLISHED / ANALOGY / SPECULATION; mandatory implications section mapping onto task IDs, roles, and the four D4 authority tiers.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE (create only this; touch no other file): docs/precedent-research/01-stare-decisis-mechanics.md. Create the parent directory with mkdir -p (idempotent and race-safe: the nine research tasks run in parallel, share no file, and no bootstrap root serializes them). Do NOT create or edit docs/precedent-research/README.md - that index is owned solely by the epic join T-348 (F1 single-owner rule).

WEB RESEARCH IS REQUIRED (coordinator decision D7): at least 5 named sources, of which at least 3 are primary (a judgment with its case name and citation, a statute or code article, an official practice statement or court rule, or a named-author treatise / peer-reviewed article). Every source is listed in a final Sources section with a retrievable identifier (case name plus citation, or URL plus retrieval date). Parametric-only claims with no locatable source are tagged SPECULATION, never ESTABLISHED.

EVERY substantive claim carries exactly one tag: ESTABLISHED (attributable to a named source in the Sources section), ANALOGY (a mapping from legal doctrine onto agent mechanics - the mapping is this agent's inference, not the source's claim), or SPECULATION (neither). An untagged substantive claim is a defect and grounds for REJECT. Basis: roadmap Part V principle 5, no fabricated rigor (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:96).

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Implications for the agent harness': map each finding onto the real substrate by name - blackboard task IDs (T-xxx), the three roles (thinker, worker, verifier) plus coordinator, and the four authority tiers of coordinator decision D4 (1 operator, 2 constitutional, 3 verdicted, 4 single-agent). For each finding state which schema field, CLI subcommand, or protocol rule it demands, or state explicitly that it demands none.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Extends, does not duplicate': for every doctrine that already has a partial implementation in this repo, cite it by file:line and say whether the finding EXTENDS the existing record or would DUPLICATE it. The candidates the scout already located: note taxonomy DECISION/DEVIATION/TRADEOFF/OPEN-QUESTION (ORCHESTRATION.md:69-77), the reopen verb with its mandatory-reasoning gate (.harness/bin/blackboard.py:470-517, ORCHESTRATION.md:58-67), the P-number ledger (state.json evolution.accepted_mutations), prose P-number citations in ORCHESTRATION.md, recontext.py append-only cited-evidence log, events.jsonl semantic event floor. Rationale: the corpus records a measured non-additive interaction where stacking one more layer that re-does existing verification REGRESSED performance (papers/agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:8, Table 3 RQ3a, '+ system_prompt only' -2.3pp; p.9 'Components interact non-additively').

MANDATORY: state at least one finding that CUTS AGAINST the roadmap brief or the coordinator decision memo where the sources support one. If the sources support none, say so explicitly and say why - a document with zero friction against its own commissioning brief is treated as unverified cheerleading.
NO CODE and NO edits under .harness/ or to PRECEDENT.md. Research tasks have no build dependencies and must create none.

Verification tier: DOC TIER per P-024 (proportional verification) - the verifier does a BRIEF replay (file exists at the exact path; every substantive claim tagged; Sources section present with the required counts; the two mandatory sections present; spot-check that 2 named sources exist), NOT a full adversarial replay. Deep evaluation of research quality happens at the synthesis tasks (T-339 / T-344) and at the epic join (T-348).
Hand off with blackboard.py handoff --to-role verifier (never self-mark done). The handoff note must name the 3 findings that most change the schema, each with the tag it carries.

MUST answer explicitly: does the D4 tier ladder (tier = how much adversarial process a decision survived: operator gate, constitutional 5A loop, producer-distinct-from-approver verdict, unverified single-agent note) behave like VERTICAL precedent, like HORIZONTAL precedent, or like neither - and name the mechanism in this repo that makes each tier observable.

MUST address where the analogy BREAKS because agents can fork at a decision point and merge branches of experience (roadmap Part V principle 4, docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:95): what does 'binding on a lineage' mean when two lineages merge, and does a merge require an adjudication step or does it silently pick a winner?

MUST state whether horizontal precedent (an agent identity bound by its OWN past decisions) is desirable here at all, given that agent identities are reassignable and reputation is per-identity (state.json agents.reputation).

notes.note: DECISION: plan is web-research common-law stare decisis (vertical/vertical hierarchy, per incuriam, panel vs en banc, coordinate/foreign persuasive line, ratio vs dicta) then map onto D4 tiers and roles; will use WebSearch/WebFetch for primary sources (named judgments, UK Practice Statement 1966, US doctrine) per D7; output docs/precedent-research/01-stare-decisis-mechanics.md only.

HANDOFF -> verifier: DECISION: doc-tier deliverable complete at docs/precedent-research/01-stare-decisis-mechanics.md (445 lines, 13 named primary sources + 2 secondary, all tagged ESTABLISHED/ANALOGY/SPECULATION). Both mandatory sections present verbatim-titled: 'Implications for the agent harness' and 'Extends, does not duplicate'. Three findings that most change the schema, each with its tag: (1) [ANALOGY] horizontal precedent doctrinally binds an OFFICE/ROLE (Young v Bristol Aeroplane; Miller v Gammie), never a reassignable identity -- cuts against coordinator memo D4's tier-3 'declared scope' wording, which does not yet specify role-scope vs identity-scope while state.json agents.reputation tracks per-identity; (2) [ESTABLISHED + ANALOGY] per incuriam (Young exception 3, [1944] KB 718) is retroactive voidance of a defective decision, not prospective overruling -- the harness's own P-025 false-green-test precedent is exactly this fact pattern, and reopen()/D4 have no status distinct from ordinary OVERRULED to capture it -- cuts against the brief's flat bind/overturn vocabulary (line 5, line 37); (3) [ESTABLISHED + ANALOGY] real precedent doctrine has zero antecedent for 'merge' of forked lineages of the SAME institution (only supersession or standing circuit-split-style plurality exists) -- cuts against Part V principle 4's framing as an open empirical question about this institution specifically; any agent merge protocol will be invented, not derived. Also answers the three MUST-answer criteria in-line under Implications: D4 tiers 1-2=vertical (fixed gate), tier 3=horizontal (self-correcting verdict), tier 4=neither (never bound); fork/merge analogy breaks because no real court forks from itself; horizontal identity-binding is doctrinally unsupported (office-binding is, identity-binding is not). Spot-checkable primary sources: Rodriguez de Quijas v. Shearson/American Express, 490 U.S. 477, 484 (1989); Practice Statement (Judicial Precedent) [1966] 1 WLR 1234.
